blocks.text: Acts 10 narrates an encounter that breaches major social and religious boundaries of early Jewish Christianity. Cornelius, a centurion stationed in Caesarea under Roman rule, and Peter, a fisherman from Galilee who became a leading witness to Jesus' resurrection, are brought together through parallel visions. The chapter unfolds through dual divine interventions—one directing Cornelius to summon Peter, another troubling Peter with a vision whose meaning remains unresolved until he enters the Gentile household itself.

sections.title: Cornelius: Centurion in Household and Empire

blocks.text: Cornelius is positioned within networks of kinship obligation and household economy that structured Mediterranean social life under imperial rule. His household—servants and soldiers dependent on his patronage and direction—would share his spiritual commitments alongside their material provisioning. The angel's command to Cornelius to summon Peter sets in motion an encounter that will test whether these household structures and ethnic divisions remain markers of separation or gates to a new community.
